Let me analyze the software specification carefully.

The specification describes a software increment for what appears to be Spring Cloud Data Flow (based on the localhost:9393 port which is Spring Cloud Data Flow's default port, and references to sinks, sources, and modules). The user stories are:

U1: File-based security configurations for endpoints (Securing Web App guide)
U2: LDAP-based security configurations for endpoints
U3: Default access control for endpoints with Admin/Viewer roles
U4: Kerberized HDFS sink (Kerberos authentication for Hadoop writes)
U5: Spike - mass-ingest data from various database systems (identify options, collaborate on design, document outcome)
U6: HBase sink (write data into HBase)
U7: File Roll sink (store events on local file system)
U8: JMX source module (publish/subscribe to JMX notifications)

HBase sink: HBase client config, Put operations, table/column family mapping. ~6-8 days.

technical_and_design_decisions: Target the existing Spring Boot / Spring Framework 6 server application (endpoints on http://localhost:9393) with Java 17 as the baseline, consistent with the specification.

Use Spring Security for U1-U3 with a pluggable authentication strategy: file-based or LDAP-based authentication selected via external configuration (properties/YAML and Spring profiles), never both simultaneously.

U1: implement file-based authentication via a custom UserDetailsService that loads users, password hashes (BCrypt), and roles from an external properties file; HTTP Basic authentication protects all REST endpoints.

U2: implement LDAP authentication using Spring Security LDAP with configurable server URL, base DN, user search filter, and group-to-role mapping; an embedded LDAP server (UnboundID) is used for automated tests.

U3: implement endpoint-level authorization rules with two roles: Admin (full read/write access) and Viewer (read-only, HTTP GET access); unmapped endpoints default to deny-all, and role rules are configurable.

U4: implement the Kerberized HDFS sink using Hadoop UserGroupInformation with keytab/principal login and a background ticket-renewal mechanism; Kerberos settings are externalized as module properties.
U6: implement the HBase sink using the HBase Java client with configurable table name, column family, row-key strategy, and payload-to-column mapping.
U7: implement the File Roll sink as a streaming file writer to the local filesystem with configurable directory, filename pattern, and rollover policies (size/time based).
U8: implement the JMX source on top of Spring Integration's JMX notification-listening channel adapter, converting JMX notifications into messages published to the bound message broker.
Package U4, U6, U7 (sinks) and U8 (source) as standalone Spring Cloud Stream application modules consistent with the existing module ecosystem.
U5 is executed as a time-boxed spike: evaluate Apache Sqoop, Kafka Connect JDBC, Debezium/CDC, and Spring Batch/Task-based ingestion; the only deliverable is a documented design specification.
Testing stack: JUnit 5, Spring Boot Test, Spring Security Test, embedded LDAP, and Apache Hadoop MiniKdc/MiniDFSCluster/HBase mini-cluster for integration tests.
assumptions: All work is performed by a single developer (myself); one workday equals 8 hours of effort. Estimates cover effort, not calendar time.
An existing, building application codebase (server exposing endpoints at localhost:9393 plus a module framework for sources/sinks) is available, including source control and CI infrastructure.
Security stories U1-U3 apply to the server's HTTP/REST endpoints only; no OAuth2/SSO, no UI work, and no changes to non-HTTP interfaces are required.
Only two roles (Admin and Viewer) are needed for U3; Viewer is read-only and Admin has full access.
A Kerberos KDC, HDFS cluster, and HBase cluster are available for manual verification; automated integration tests rely on embedded/mini clusters instead.
U5 produces research findings and a design document only; no production code for mass-ingestion is implemented in this increment.
U5 evaluation is limited to common relational databases (Oracle, MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server) as the ingestion sources.
The existing jdbchdfs approach remains unchanged and in place.
Documentation effort is limited to reference documentation and module README updates; no separate user guide or training material is produced.
No dedicated performance/load testing, penetration testing, or external security audit is included beyond developer-level sanity testing.
Third-party dependencies (Spring Security, Spring Integration, Hadoop/HBase client libraries) are readily available from internal or public repositories.

activities.activity_name: Requirements analysis and overall technical design
activities.activity_description: Analyze U1-U8, design the security architecture (authentication/authorization model), module layouts for the new sinks/source, and the Kerberos integration approach; produce a brief design note.

activities.activity_name: Build and project setup for new modules
activities.activity_description: Create build descriptors, module skeletons, dependency management, and CI pipeline updates for the four new modules (Kerberized HDFS sink, HBase sink, File Roll sink, JMX source) and security changes.
Implement file-based UserDetailsService, password encoding, security properties, and Spring Security filter chain protecting all server endpoints; wire configuration toggle.
Unit and integration tests covering successful/failed authentication, endpoint protection, and configuration loading for file-based security.
Implement LDAP authentication provider with configurable URL, base DN, user search, and group/role mapping as an alternative to file-based security.
Unit and integration tests against an embedded LDAP server (LDIF fixtures) covering authentication success/failure and role resolution.

activities.activity_name: U3 - Default role-based access control implementation
activities.activity_description: Implement endpoint authorization rules mapping Admin (full access) and Viewer (read-only) roles across all listed endpoints, with configurable defaults and deny-by-default behavior.
Tests verifying role-to-endpoint mappings, forbidden/allowed combinations for Admin and Viewer, and default rules.
Implement HDFS sink write path plus Kerberos support: keytab/principal login via UserGroupInformation, JAAS configuration, and ticket renewal; externalize all settings as module properties.
Unit tests plus integration tests using MiniKdc and MiniDFSCluster to verify authenticated writes and renewal behavior.
Implement HBase sink with configurable table, column family, row-key strategy, and payload mapping to Put operations, including connection management and error handling.
Unit tests and integration tests against an HBase mini-cluster verifying writes, mapping logic, and failure handling.
Implement sink writing incoming events to local filesystem files with configurable directory, filename pattern, and rollover policies.
Unit and integration tests for file creation, rollover behavior, naming, and content integrity.
Implement JMX source module using Spring Integration JMX notification-listening adapter: MBean subscription configuration, notification-to-message conversion, and publication to the message broker.
Unit and integration tests with a local MBean server verifying notification receipt, conversion, and message publication.

activities.activity_name: U5 - Spike: research mass-ingestion integration options
activities.activity_description: Investigate and prototype-evaluate options (Apache Sqoop, Kafka Connect JDBC, Debezium/CDC, Spring Batch/Task) for ingesting data from various database systems without JDBC-driver coupling.

activities.activity_name: U5 - Spike: design collaboration and documentation
activities.activity_description: Consolidate findings, hold design review/collaboration session, and produce the documented design specification with a recommended approach.
Cross-feature verification: secured endpoints under both authentication modes with both roles, and end-to-end stream runs exercising the new sink/source modules.
Document security configuration (file/LDAP, roles), new module properties and usage for the Kerberized HDFS, HBase, File Roll sinks and JMX source; include U5 design doc in the docs set.

activities.activity_name: Code review, rework, and release preparation
activities.activity_description: Self-review and peer-style review pass, defect fixing and rework, final build verification, and release preparation of the increment.
